title: Breaking and Entering: Dick Diver
summary: Two of the members from Dick Diver – Steph Hughes and Al Montfort – delve into their feelings of anticipation regarding their upcoming shows at the Thornbury Theatre, sharing details of the line up and potential future gigs! They also discuss the experience of being reunited with the band and playing together again, 10 years after their last album release, while also reminising on their time in the music industry over the years.
transcript:
A conversation with Dick Diver about their reunion shows, broadcast on Breaking and Entering, Triple R, 22 May 2025.

[Unclear audio at 00:00:18.420–00:02:41.900]

Of course, Dick Diver there with 'Alice'. An incredible song from an incredible band. And as promised, we're thrilled to be joined by two members of the band. Welcome to Al Montfort and Steph Hughes of Dick Diver. Thank you so much for being here with us.

Thank you for having us. This is great.

Thanks for letting us come back in again.

Oh, absolutely any time. A band that really absolutely needs no introduction. But I suppose, just for a little bit of background and context, there were the initial EPs that you released, and you formed, I suppose, back in 2008. There was the real breakthrough debut, New Start Again, that we were talking with Guy and Ben about from Chapter Music, such a landmark release. Then Calendar Days, and 2015's Melbourne, Florida, which was 10 years ago, which seems surreal. But of course, all releases that made such a huge impact, have an incredible legacy, continue to remain influential and are just beloved classics. So we're thrilled to hear that you've announced some upcoming shows. Hope you're feeling the love from everyone too, because there's just a collective excitement around it.

[Unclear audio at 00:03:55.300–00:03:56.580]

Yeah, it's been pretty wild. I think, you know, how we operate, we really just kind of have to seize the moment when the bandmates are around. It's such a special event in itself just when all our bandmates are in the same place at the same time, and the fact that, you know, everyone else has got around it too. That was a great bonus.

Oh, fantastic.

And we're like, might as well add a couple more shows. It's going to be four days in, yeah, the Thornbury Theatre now.

I think we saw on socials, is it [name uncertain: Tom Lincoln] calling for some kind of Las Vegas-style residency? We just want every night for a month.

That's what I'm aiming for, yeah. Some dances and stuff.

Absolutely. Well, I guess, yeah, Simon mentioned it's been 10 years since your most recent Dick Diver album, Melbourne, Florida, and you mentioned that now felt like the right time for these shows. What sort of sparked the reunion?

[Unclear audio at 00:04:50.360–00:04:51.400]

I think, like Steph said, just being all in the same city. I think we'd feel — well, it's great to just play together and see each other, but also I'd feel pretty guilty if we didn't play, and [unclear 00:05:06.620–00:05:08.940]. I think the, yeah, Melbourne [wording unclear: “Django Chorus”] community would be really angry.

It would have been an outrage.

Detained, citizen's arrest.

It's a guilt and a shame-based reunion, yeah, as always.

Powerful motivators.

Yeah, biggest motivator for us is definitely shame.

Always.

That's so funny. Well, it's joy. Joy is the overriding emotion, that's for sure, from all the fans and ourselves and listeners. Thinking about the fact that in August there will be, yeah, Friday, Saturday and Sunday, four shows, some all-ages, which we'll, I suppose, talk about in a little bit. But I guess the music itself obviously speaks across generations, when they were released, and are resonant still. I suppose for yourselves as, you know, members of the band during rehearsals, looking back on the album, sort of what feelings are emerging as you're sort of revisiting the catalogue?

[Unclear audio at 00:06:01.680–00:06:03.800]

We've had a couple of jams with, yeah, just Steph, Al and myself, because we're all in Melbourne at the moment. And it's been kind of amazing, like playing the songs again.

Instant, yeah.

Instant, yeah. We just kind of, yeah, bit of muscle memory in there. But also I think afterwards, yeah, joy, joy, less shame, more joy.

Less shame, yeah.

When we were jamming, I think, yeah, it felt pretty special.

Totally. And I guess those songs really evoke a particular period, maybe for you as a band, but do they sort of resonate in new and surprising ways now as well?

Yeah, they do to me. I think that, you know, you go on, it's so joyous, you know, like all bands are kind of like little teams a bit. And I think that they all have, you know, different dynamics and stuff. And I think with Dick Diver, it is seriously like riding a bike. Like I think we really connect very easily with certain melodies and like harmonies and the way that we sync together, the way our instruments play together. And, you know, I suppose we played together so much at such a time, you know, like 15 years ago we played together so much, that it really is a part of how we all play music now. Like, you know, what we take to other bands and what we take, you know, playing in the world. So, yeah, it really brings up — kind of some of those things are more highlighted for me now that I've just played music in different spaces, yeah.

And yet it is so joyous. Like I was like, oh, this is amazing, you know, seeing Al again, because Al McKay, one of our guitarists, has moved back to Melbourne. So, yeah, it's hopefully less of a rare thing to be able to all be together now. But, yeah, he was in London for 10 years.

Great to have him back. Well, I guess it's been a bit of a reflective show for us today. We spoke to Guy and Ben of Chapter Music earlier about their show at Rising. It's a sort of end of an era for the label and a beginning of a new one. And, of course, you've released your albums on Chapter as well. Can you tell us more about your relationship with that label?

[Unclear audio at 00:08:22.540–00:08:24.240]

Yeah, I'm trying to think. Yeah, Guy and Ben came to an early show.

The [venue name uncertain: Burmy].

The [venue name uncertain: Burmy], yeah.

Yeah, we supported Guy Blackman, I think.

Oh, yes, yes, yes. So they were there.

Guy was there anyway.

He had to be there.

We just crashed it.

Exactly, yeah. I think we were in the right spot, and we played with Guy and it was Sly Hats as well.

Oh, true. Yeah, Geoffrey O'Connor's other band other than Crayon Fields.

That's right, Crayon Fields.

Crayon Fields, yes.

[Unclear audio at 00:08:51.600–00:08:53.220]

But the [venue name uncertain: Burmy].

Yeah. What an era.

[Unclear audio at 00:08:55.880–00:08:57.880]

I think, yeah, maybe the relationship over time has been pretty involved for a label. I think, yeah, they like to discuss the finer points of releases. I think I heard on the interview earlier, Ben was talking about sequences.

Yes.

And I think we've got our own ideas, and it's always good to get their input.

Yeah. But we're probably annoying for them as well.

No, I'm sure they appreciate the decisiveness.

[Unclear audio at 00:09:34.840–00:09:36.100]

Yeah.

[Unclear audio at 00:09:36.480–00:09:37.540]

So, I guess, what have Chapter meant to you in terms of the broader musical community of the city?

Yeah, I think I was thinking about that before, when you asked about coming back, what spurred these shows. I think being a part of this community, being a part of, you know, RRR, PBS, 3CR, a part of the Melbourne music community, people that we've met through Chapter, everybody on Chapter.

Totally.

I think it's really important. I would feel — when I say I would feel guilt and shame if we didn't play, maybe back to shame.

It's a bit of a pattern, yeah.

I think it would be, yeah, I think it's as much for all our friends and all our, you know, fellow community members as well as for ourselves. And I think, like, when we ended up releasing music on Chapter, we were sort of instantly a part, instantly embedded in a lot of amazing communities that Guy and Ben had kind of, you know, paved before. So, you know, that's initially why I think we've all connected at the start. And, yeah, super grateful for that kind of community work that has been done by them.

Absolutely. And it is, yeah, it's a community, and it's like, yeah, feel so lucky.

Completely. It's so aligned, yeah, what Chapter are doing and what yourselves are doing as, I suppose, interconnected parts of that larger extended family. It is really beautiful to see. And it's very much going to be a family affair during these shows.

Has to be.

We saw 18-plus, but of course, all-ages as well. That must have been important because it would be a whole new generation who've kind of discovered you through their family's CD collections and records.

I hope so, yeah. I think it's a bit of a — it's actually a bit of a childcare co-op scenario that we've got going on, because there's multiple kids involved. And I've got one in here in the studio right now who's doing a great job, just quality control.

It's a great time sitting with us.

Yeah, she's hanging out.

[Unclear audio at 00:11:47.260–00:11:48.440]

But yeah, I think we all just wanted to be able to — a lot of our friends with kids — we just wanted it all to be a big sort of, you know, gathering for everyone who can.

I guess the Dick Diver live shows, so much excitement from everyone sort of getting to see you play again. There's that famous story of people jumping the fence one year, I think, at Laneway Festival during your set. We're going to, I don't know, expect something similar this time perhaps.

Yeah, they weren't jumping the fence to see us.

That's unconfirmed.

[Unclear audio at 00:12:21.560–00:12:22.800]

Vance Joy was playing on the stage, I think, next to us.

[Unclear audio at 00:12:25.700–00:12:27.020]

Renowned sweetie though, Vance Joy at the airport lounge. I was like, this guy is a legend.

Absolute legend, yeah. And so we were like, fair enough. Run past us.

A few stops, a few stops.

[Unclear audio at 00:12:39.720–00:12:41.280]

Can we ask about the line-up and who you've invited? Because we've just announced actually another show today that's happening at the Thornbury Theatre, an all-ages show on Sunday, August 3rd. Can you talk us through, yeah, who you've invited to play with you?

[Unclear audio at 00:12:56.880–00:12:58.080]

August 3rd. I think that's the Sunday arvo.

Sunday arvo.

Yeah, Kankawa, yeah.

Yeah, Kankawa Nagarra. So, yeah, she's travelling. Well, where do I start? We're such fans. Her record, Wirlmarni, that came out — well, it must have been last year, because it won the Australian Music Prize last year —

[Unclear audio at 00:13:19.460–00:13:20.540]

— has just been non-stop for me. I love it so much. She just writes really sort of timeless and intuitive tracks. So she's coming all the way from the Kimberley, and I think it's about 100K outside of Fitzroy Crossing. It's an extremely long distance to get to us. But, yeah, Al's — and you've done a lot of amazing booking work — and I think we've got her coming down. And she's supported by — or she's accompanied by — our friend Darren Hanlon, who has done a lot of sort of touring with her in the outback, and they're about to go to Europe together. So, yeah, she's 80 years old, and apparently she's just really keen to do all these adventures. Because I was like, maybe she might be tired, or maybe she might, you know, want to do some other stuff local to home, and he's like, nah, she's frothing. So she's ready to go. And, yeah, she's also played a couple of times with Darren's kids. So I know, yeah, she's just great for like older folks, younger folks. She's just an incredible performer. So stoked.

Definitely. And I guess no shame or expectation with this next question, but I suppose we're so excited that there has been this sort of reunion, and obviously now that it's a bit easier to get together, are there sort of thoughts of what's maybe on the horizon in terms of other gigs or future releases potentially?

[Unclear audio at 00:14:54.380–00:14:56.160]

There's, yeah, a record that's nearly finished. I think this is a shame thing on me because I'm definitely one of the handbrakes.

No shame in the —

It's a shame-free space.

It's a shame-free space, yeah.

You can hold the shame stick now.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. [Unclear wording] Yeah, there is a shame stick. For those listening at home, which I think most of you are, there's a shame stick here.

But that's incredible news for us to hear. So that's sort of, yeah, something you've been working on.

Yeah. Working on.

It's been a fair while. So it was sort of like the last time we were able to hang out in real life that we put the bones of it together, and then it's just been overdubbing and — but yeah, a couple of, kind of, kids and life and all that stuff. And then I think that, yeah, I feel super motivated to get it out one day.

Yeah, watch this space.

This is great news.

We've got lots there, and any time we're ever together, I think we'd like to play gigs.

[Unclear audio at 00:15:53.380–00:15:54.140]

It's just natural that we feel like it. So yeah, we're all really good friends, you know.

Yeah, fantastic. Well, we're all absolutely rapt that Dick Diver are back playing shows, new album on the way.

[Unclear audio at 00:16:06.700–00:16:07.720]

The shows are Friday the 1st of August — they're all at Thornbury Theatre — Friday the 1st of August with Workhorse. The two shows on the Saturday, are they both sold out?

Yes. I believe, yeah.

[Unclear audio at 00:16:17.460–00:16:18.940]

And as we mentioned, on Sunday, August 3rd at Thornbury Theatre as well, an all-ages show which has just been announced this morning with Kankawa Nagarra. You'd want to get on that for tickets. I'm sure that will sell out as well. It's been awesome having you guys back with us in the studio after all these years.

So nice. Thank you.

We're going to play another track from Dick Diver. This is 'New Start Again'. Thank you so much, Steph and Al, for joining us.

Thank you.

Thanks.

[Unclear audio at 00:16:49.640–00:19:29.320]

[Unclear audio at 00:19:43.380–00:20:00.043]
